messages.subject: Equality constraint syntax
parts:
On the midterm exam in my class, I gave students a model and a dataset with missing data.  Besides its other features, the model specified an equality constraint for two parameters--reciprocal relations linking factors F4 and F5.  My version of the syntax for this was:
'
          F1 =~ Y1+Y2+Y3
          F2 =~ Y4
          F3 =~ Y5+Y6
          F4 =~ Y7+Y8+Y9
          F5 =~ Y10+Y11

          F5 ~ mike*F4+F1
          F4 ~ mike*F5+F2+F3

          F4 ~~F5
          F1 ~~0*F3
          F2 ~~0*F3
          Y4~~0.20*Y4
'
     With the sem function and missing = "FIML" I got the expected result--the simulated data fits this model well.
     One of my students specified the equality constraint differently:
'
          F5 ~ b1*F4+F1
          F4 ~ b2*F5+F2+F3

          b1 == b2
'
     This specification produced error messages.  The parameters constrained to equality went to an extreme value (-1.001) such that Sigma-hat was not positive definite.

     Should the student's syntax have worked?  I am attaching the data file, which has 999 for a missing value code.  The file also has an extra 12th column of 1s.
--Ed Rigdon

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Equality constraint syntax
parts:
Hi Ed,

I've run into a similar issue before and as I recall the issue is in the optimizer lavaan uses. Once you introduce "complex" constraints (e.g. including ==, <, > etc.) into the model lavaan will switch optimizers. I tried to find which optimizer it is using in each case using your example, but I couldn't dig it out. I'm hoping Yves will chime in on that :). The constrained optimizer is a bit finickier (e.g. sensitive to start values) than the unconstrained optimizer and that might explain the issue.

Alex

messages.subject: Re: Equality constraint syntax
parts:
Alex--
     Thanks very much!  More than one SEM package has run into problems where equality constraints conflict with other constraints in a model, like the factor scaling constraints that lavaan imposes here.  The "same label" syntax for imposing an equality constraint works beautifully in this case, but then, that approach would not extend to inequality or anything more general.
--Ed Rigdon

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Equality constraint syntax
parts:
> I've run into a similar issue before and as I recall the issue is in
> the optimizer lavaan uses. Once you introduce "complex" constraints
> (e.g. including ==, <, > etc.) into the model lavaan will switch
> optimizers. I tried to find which optimizer it is using in each case
> using your example, but I couldn't dig it out. I'm hoping Yves will
> chime in on that :).

<Chime in>
This is 100% correct (for the current version of lavaan, 0.5-14): as
soon as "==" or "<" or ">" statements are added to the model syntax,
lavaan 'switches' to the constrained optimizer (nlminb.constr), which is
very, very sensitive to starting values.

This was in fact designed to handle ugly highly-nonlinear (in)equality
constraints, like b1 == exp(b2)^2 + log(b3 + b4).

What lavaan is not doing (yet), is to 'catch' simple linear equality
constraints (like b1 == 2*b2), because in this case, we can simply
reduce the problem using a projection matrix, and everything will run
smoothly. This is happening already when we have 'equal labels', but we
need to extend this to all linear equality constraints (specified by
using the '==' operator). More work to do.
</Chime in>

Yves.
